summary.short: EU regulation designating large online platform undertakings as gatekeepers for ten core platform services and imposing conduct obligations on them (data combination, self-preferencing, interoperability, data access, sideloading). The Commission enforces it with fines up to 10% (20% for repeat) of worldwide turnover. Applies from 2 May 2023.
summary.long: The Regulation covers core platform services gatekeepers offer to Union business or end users, wherever the gatekeeper is established. An undertaking is designated a gatekeeper if it has significant impact on the internal market, operates an important gateway and holds an entrenched position; these are presumed where it has EUR 7.5 billion annual Union turnover in each of three years or EUR 75 billion market capitalisation, serves at least three Member States, and a service has 45 million monthly active end users and 10 000 yearly active business users in each of the last three years (Annex methodology). Undertakings meeting the thresholds must notify within two months and may rebut the presumption; the Commission may also designate through market investigation. Within six months of designation gatekeepers must comply with Articles 5-7 (consent for data combination, no parity clauses, anti-steering, choice screens, sideloading, ranking neutrality, interoperability, data portability and access), report, submit audited profiling descriptions, notify concentrations and set up a compliance function. The Commission may impose fines up to 10% of worldwide turnover (20% for repeat, 1% for procedural breaches), periodic penalties up to 5% of daily turnover, and remedies for systematic non-compliance.

territorial_scope.description: Directly applicable in all Member States; covers core platform services offered to business users established, or end users established or located, in the Union irrespective of where the gatekeeper is established.

notes: Neutral annotation of the DMA as consolidated (000.002) with Corrigendum C1, which adds Art. 13(8). Dates: entry into force is computed as 2022-11-01 (20th day after OJ publication on 2022-10-12), consistent with Art. 49(2) ('5 years from 1 November 2022'); the general application date is 2 May 2023. The registry record's dates.entry_into_force (2023-05-02) is the application date, not entry into force (resolve stage). Legislative dates come from OJ footnote 3 (EP position 5 July 2022; Council decision 18 July 2022). The registry's 'adopted' 2022-09-14 equals the signature date. Text inconsistencies: Arts 51 and 52 cite the DMA as 'OJ L 265, 21.9.2022, p. 1', while the act was published in OJ L 265 of 12.10.2022; Art. 3(3) third subpara. refers to 'the request for information pursuant to the second subparagraph', which itself refers to Art. 21; Art. 17(1) has a comma where a full stop is expected. Coding choices: the Art. 3(2)(a) turnover test uses Union (not worldwide) turnover and is coded as revenue_annual; yearly active business users and the three-year persistence test use 'other'. Gatekeeper duties are coded with addressee platform_operator (undertaking providing core platform services); OS/browser/virtual-assistant-specific duties use browser_os_provider and search-specific duties search_engine_operator. Cloud computing services are a core platform service (Art. 2(2)(i)) but carry no cloud-specific obligations. Business users, app developers and NIICS rivals have no addressee role and are described in summaries. Commission powers under Arts 16-25 and 29 are reflected in obligations, events and enforcement; commitments (Art. 25) and specification decisions (Art. 8) are not sanctions. private_right_of_action is null for Commission sanction rows: the text neither creates nor excludes individual actions; Art. 39 refers to national court proceedings applying the Regulation, and Art. 42 applies the Representative Actions Directive (coded true on that row). No firms are named: gatekeepers are designated by separate Commission decisions (registry: eu-dma-gatekeeper-designations), and the procedural implementing regulation (eu-dma-procedural-2023) is not referenced in this text. No AI-specific provisions; virtual assistants and cloud computing services appear only as core platform service categories. National competition authorities are designated generically, not named.
